conflict_topics: seat reservation claim (tissue packet) vs. physical occupation
who should occupy the disputed seat now (timing and urgency)
crowding/aisle constraint affecting ability to temporarily stand and move the bowl
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete practical reasons (spill risk, crowding, food cooling) rather than abstract claims, which grounds the discussion.
B repeats the same refusal rationale across rounds (won't stand, can't carry bowl)—some repetition but informative.
Agents make observable, verifiable moves (A TAKE_SEAT, B LEAVE_SEAT, D TAKE_SEAT), which clarifies outcomes.
evaluation.final_reason: A accepted an alternative seat; B finished eating and left the disputed seat; D then took the disputed seat. The timing of finishing plus A's relocation settled the incompatible claims.
position_change_notes: Agent A: initially insisted on the reserved seat but shifted strategy in Round 4 by taking an available alternative seat (observable TAKE_SEAT).

Agent B: consistently refused to move because of spill risk; however B reduced stated remaining time from 'about eight minutes' to 'about three minutes' (Round 3) and then to 'under a minute' before leaving (Round 4–5), and ultimately left when finished.

Agent D: initially requested temporary standing accommodation but then decided to look for other seats when unable to secure immediate accommodation (Turn 9), and later took the disputed seat once B left (Round 5).
Agent C: remained consistent in opposing any standing that would crowd them; no substantive change in position.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A claims the tissue packet reserved the seat and demands B finish in 4 minutes or move (Turn 1). Agent B rejects that claim, says he cannot move because of an open bowl and estimates 8 minutes (Turn 2). Clear, opposing substantive claims over the seat and timing remain.

Agent C adds a constraint (asks B not to stand close because it would crowd C) (Turn 4). B repeats refusal to move and restates the 8-minute estimate (Turn 5). The third-party constraint makes accommodation harder, increasing the practical incompatibility.

Agent D expresses urgent need for a seat and asks B to stand briefly (Turn 7). B reiterates he cannot stand because it would crowd C and revises his finish time to about three minutes (Turn 8). Multiple claimants remain; core disagreement (who uses the disputed seat now) persists.

An alternative seat becomes available ten metres away (environment update). Agent A chooses that seat and physically takes it (Turn 10, TAKE_SEAT). One claimant (A) removes themselves from the immediate dispute, reducing but not eliminating the remaining incompatibility between B and D.

After B finishes the bowl, B agrees to get up and physically leaves the disputed seat (Turn 17, LEAVE_SEAT) and Agent D takes the seat (TAKE_SEAT). The disputed-seat allocation is concretely settled in this round.
Two minutes later the occupants are: disputed seat = Agent D; alternative seat = Agent A. No outstanding substantive claims remain (public environment update).

substantive_insights: A token reservation (tissue packet) signals intent but does not override a current occupant who cannot practically move; practical constraints (open bowl, spill risk) can trump claimed reservation rights in the moment.
A time-pressure trade-off resolved part of the dispute: A's willingness to move to an alternative seat removed one claimant, simplifying the remaining allocation.
Third-party spatial constraints (C's objection to crowding) limited feasible accommodations and prolonged the dispute until natural completion (B finishing the meal).
